conditions: Another GPU workload (krea2-nnan/krea2-final) was active. Interleaved arms alternate order within a process on one shared generated corpus. No other hrxdb GPU work ran concurrently; clocks and competing load were not controlled. Retain all samples. Compare arms within each run, not absolute times across runs.
interpretation: Host samples measure completed ordinary searches, excluding ingestion, reservation, compilation, and profiling. Three warmups precede each series.

Three separately instrumented replays per arm follow all ordinary samples; each is checked against that arm's ordinary results. Their stage intervals include instrumentation and contention; they are not components of ordinary latency.
All compared neighbor IDs and score bits match; final-tile comparisons include padded query slots. Corpora <=262144 rows compare the entire score matrix.
Detailed report counts are static compiler evidence, not dynamic hardware counters. Register counts, peak live units, and rounded residency allocation are distinct metrics.
ISA counts count one dual-FMAC instruction for two arithmetic terms. Counts refer to one static unrolled 32-component loop body, not the dynamic instruction total for a query.

Representative width-64/dimension-384 compiler reports below are complete. Other runs retain resource, allocation, emission and wait summaries. Profile samples retain device summary and per-stage intervals; full per-command ticks/geometry are reproducible with the harness.

Exploration variants were generated locally. fenceN widens the original per-column fence interval; open removes fences; open-unroll also unrolls staging; dotN uses N ordered products over open-unroll. dot16-vs8 and dot32-vs8 use the selected dot8 as baseline.

The initial dot8 experiments spell out tile loads. The final source uses equivalent shaped vectors/unrolled loops. All three width-64/dimension-384 executables have identical SHA256 despite distinct source/cache digests; initial run source digests remain unchanged in this record.
